newsitem.title: ITALY: Fiat says strike effect less than September.
newsitem.headline: Fiat says strike effect less than September.

text.p: Italy's automotive group Fiat said 10 percent less of its total workforce had joined in a national strike of engineering and metalworkers on Friday compared with a similar one-day strike on September 27.

According to figures from Fiat, its giant Mirafiori car plant in Turin saw 19 percent of the workforce striking in its car body shop, 29 percent on its assembly lines, and 18 percent in its press works.

At its southern Italian car factory, Bravo/Brava plant Cassino showed a stiking level of 26 percent, Alfa Romeo factory Pomigliano d'Arco near Naples some 25 percent and Melfi, which produces the Punto and Lancia Y, 23 percent.
But in certain areas the strike levels were higher than in September. At trucks unit Iveco, the striking level was 80 percent and at aerospace group Fiat Avio some 67 percent.

Contracts for some 1.7 million metal and engineering workers expired at the end of June but employers and unions since then have failed to agree on new terms and this situation has developed into an increasingly bitter pay dispute.
